There is a countertop version and a version that can be mounted on a wall. The HomeView will be available for purchase starting on November 13.

tech.title: SpaceX Plan to Launch 456 Starships a Year in Texas Under Review
tech.summary: SpaceX plans to perform as many as 456 launches and 912 landings at its Texas facility each year. The company's CEO, Elon Musk, has been open about the company's intent to launch Starship as rapidly as possible in the future. He has claimed that, in less than a decade, SpaceX will be able to launch Starship more than once every hour. SpaceX recently announced plans to invest as much as $100 billion to build a massive launch site in southern Louisiana to support rapid Starship launches.

tech.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
tech.summary: Science Corporation's vision-restoring chip, PRIMA, is commercially available in Europe for patients who have lost their sight to an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration, but the company believes its approach can be applied to multiple diseases. It recently implanted the chip in a patient with Stargardt disease, an inherited eye disease that gradually destroys central vision. The company's work with PRIMA is part of a broader pursuit of a novel brain-computer interface. It envisions a future where BCIs expand into a wide range of medical technology applications rather than just being used to control computers.

tech.title: Is all that AI coding actually worth it?
tech.summary: Span is the engineering intelligence platform that tracks AI code from prompt to prod. It connects coding agent sessions to tickets, PRs, and prod outcomes to give you the evidence you need to measure returns and pinpoint areas for improvement. tech.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
tech.summary: Anthropic was being bottlenecked by developer infrastructure built for human scale, so it built an in-house version control system called Scion to support its next stage of growth, and fully migrated its monorepo from git in five months. It also built and shipped a code review surface, code search, a rich source control IAM system, novel ways of managing and landing large amounts of reviewed code, and more, all in that same time period. Anthropic averaged about 2,500 code changes merged per day in May. It now merges over 30,000 per day, and the rate of growth isn't expected to slow down anytime soon.

tech.title: How to be more ambitious: A tutorial for humans with models
tech.summary: There are four types of ambition. Speed gets the same work done in less time. Altitude involves going up in abstraction and considering the outcome rather than the individual task. Depth considers a task the way a field-leading expert would, going one level deeper and touching the underlying data, tools, and problems. Range draws on multiple fields rather than just the one the task might need at the surface using knowledge, tools, and techniques you normally wouldn't.

tech.title: Were we blue-collar workers all along?
tech.summary: Blue-collar workers typically do the hands-on labor of making or fixing stuff. Software developers have tried to separate themselves from this category, but they also make or fix stuff, just in bits rather than atoms. Just like electricians or carpenters, software developers must spend years practicing their craft in order to become skilled and sought-after. Just like anyone else in a skilled trade, software engineers can be outpaced by technology.

tech.title: FBI Arrests OpenAI Employee Accused of Planting Bug in Office

It was traced to Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi Arabian national who joined the company's product team in July 2025 as an engineer. He was arrested by the FBI. The device was built to evade detection and used advanced encryption. It could monitor audio and had a way to transfer data without being noticed.

ai.title: Gemini 4 Argon Lands on Google Cloud
ai.summary: Google made Gemini 4 Argon available on Google Cloud as a frontier model for long, multi-step enterprise work. It was positioned for tasks requiring sustained context and domain expertise, including software development, finance, legal work, and cybersecurity.

ai.title: Arguments About AI Consciousness Remain Highly Motivated and At Best Overconfident
ai.summary: The debate over AI consciousness continues with minimal progress, as many argue without strong evidence. Anthropic's new policy classifies abusive behavior towards AI, such as Claude, as a violation of terms to cultivate positive model interactions. Despite skepticism from many, some, including Nick Bostrom, believe current AIs may be conscious, complicating ethical considerations around AI development.

ai.title: How Anthropic's Dynamic Workflows Coordinate Claude Agents
ai.summary: Splitting a task among several AI agents creates another job: deciding who does what, passing information between them, and checking their results. Anthropic's dynamic workflows let Claude write the program that manages those steps. An October 12 demonstration assigned stock tickers to separate agents, then reviewed their findings before producing a report. The presenters said this found more detail but cost much more than using one agent. Developers can set a session spending limit, but the running model does not know that budget.

Users just upload data, launch fine-tuning on managed compute and infrastructure, and access the fine-tuned models via a hosted gateway to run inference.

ai.title: OpenCode 2.0

Programmatic clients will autodiscover the local service and just work. OpenCode can now be used as a library with the SDK package. More details about the update are available in the article.

ai.title: Ramp Glass

webdev.title: Rewinding the Exponential: How We Keep Hardware Usage Down
webdev.summary: Cloudflare's data pipeline handles roughly two billion events per second while hardware capacity grows more slowly than traffic. Product-specific schemas, zstd compression, later replication, earlier sampling, and aggregation have collectively deferred the equivalent of two and a half years of hardware expansion.

webdev.title: Redesigning Source Control at Anthropic
webdev.summary: Anthropic replaced Git with Scion after daily merges grew from roughly 2,500 to more than 30,000. The centralized system uses server-side commits, sparse checkouts, and layered caches, reducing its source control infrastructure's CPU and memory footprint by 200 times and freeing 25% of CI CPU capacity.

webdev.title: A Year of Fast Apply: The Path to 10k Tokens per Second
webdev.summary: Relace explains how it built a small model that applies code edits at a reported 10,000 tokens per second using high-quality merge data, LoRA fine-tuning, FP8 quantization, and speculative decoding. Its training pipeline filtered 200,000 candidate examples down to about 145,000, using a judge calibrated against 500 manually reviewed merges. Relace Apply 3 supports a 256,000-token context and multiple diff formats, although improving frontier-model edit accuracy could eventually reduce the need for specialized apply models.

webdev.title: Recreational Programming
webdev.summary: Programming for curiosity and enjoyment can restore motivation without requiring a business case or a finished product. This presentation suggests small experiments, toy implementations, language exploration, and documenting the process, with permission to switch projects or stop when they stop being fun.

webdev.title: How to Be More Ambitious: A Tutorial for Humans with Models
webdev.summary: More ambitious AI use can mean pursuing higher-level outcomes, applying expert methods to raw data, or combining ideas from multiple fields. Practical examples show how to move beyond generating a quarterly slide deck toward identifying urgent decisions, testing assumptions, and validating results with independent tools.

webdev.title: AI agents are the primary readers of Mintlify-powered sites.
webdev.summary: In August, agents made 257 million web requests versus 131 million human page loads, nearly 2:1. The report covers what that means for how you write and maintain docs. Read the report

webdev.title: TanStack Start 1.0 Is Stable
webdev.summary: TanStack Start 1.0 is now stable and ready for production, formalizing a commitment to its APIs after extensive real-world use. It combines type-safe routing with server rendering, typed server functions, and middleware spanning client and server, while shipping current agent guidance through TanStack Intent.

webdev.title: Gemini 4 Argon
webdev.summary: Google DeepMind introduces Gemini 4 Argon for complex software engineering, scientific research, robotics, and professional workflows. The model offers a one-million-token output window, and Google reports uses ranging from large Chromium refactors to physics-ready robot simulations and vulnerability remediation.

webdev.title: Frontier Models for Every Robot: Announcing the Pi API Beta
webdev.summary: Physical Intelligence's API beta lets developers upload robot demonstrations, fine-tune its models on managed infrastructure, and run inference through a hosted gateway. Early partners independently improved policies across manufacturing and other applications, although some deployments exposed network connectivity challenges.

webdev.title: The “Alien” Economics of AI Monetization
webdev.summary: Two-thirds of the Forbes AI 50 companies use some form of usage-based pricing as variable AI costs push businesses toward hybrid subscriptions, credits, and outcome charges. Examples from AI companies show why spending controls, flexible packaging, measurable customer value, and pricing pages readable by both people and agents are becoming part of the product.

webdev.summary: Federal prosecutors charged an OpenAI engineer with using or attempting to use a device to intercept conversations after a concealed recorder was found in an executive conference room. OpenAI says it referred the discovery to the FBI and has found no indication that model weights, source code, or customer data were improperly accessed or taken.

webdev.title: Are Harnesses Worth the Cost?
webdev.summary: In ten runs on one Java API service, a behavioral harness raised GPT-6 Luna's acceptance rate from three successes to ten, while GPT-6 Sol passed all ten runs with or without it. Harnessed Luna cost about 33% less per run than unharnessed Sol, but those estimates exclude harness maintenance and the unusually detailed brief limits how broadly the results apply.

webdev.title: I Posted to HN, and Then My Website Was Flooded with AI Bot Traffic
webdev.summary: After a Hacker News post, heavy automated traffic slowed a feed reader, prompting endpoint logging, blocking an aggressive scraper, rate limits, and infrastructure improvements.

webdev.title: Bifrost

infosec.title: GitLab Patches CVSS 10.0 Flaw That Could Let Unauthenticated Users Run Server Code
infosec.summary: GitLab fixed CVE-2026-97229, a CVSS 10.0 integer overflow vulnerability in regex validation for CI/CD configurations. In certain conditions, an unauthenticated user could execute arbitrary code on a GitLab server. The fixes are included in CE/EE versions 19.2.8, 19.3.5, and 19.4.2. The release also addresses high-severity XSS, authorization, and response-cache poisoning vulnerabilities.

infosec.title: Owner of fashion brands Hobbs and Whistles joins autumn pwned collection
infosec.summary: TFG London, owner of Hobbs, Phase Eight, and Whistles, detected a cyberattack on October 11. Several IT systems remain offline, website functions are limited, and orders placed on or after Sunday may be delayed. TFG has not found evidence that payment data was exposed. It is still checking whether customer data was compromised. Attack method, ransomware involvement, and restoration timing remain undisclosed.

infosec.title: Ghostscript Flaw Lets Hackers Hijack Servers via PDF Uploads
infosec.summary: Wordfence discovered a new vulnerability in the Ghostscript interpreter and rendering engine which could allow attackers to achieve remote code execution (RCE) using specially crafted PDFs. For WordPress sites to be vulnerable, an attacker must be able to upload PDFs which are then processed by a vulnerable version of Ghostscript to generate a preview or thumbnail. Other applications that use Ghostscript to generate previews or thumbnails from PDFs may also be vulnerable.

infosec.title: Playing It SFAPE: Code Execution in Isolated User Mode
infosec.summary: Doyensec found a chain in Windows' SFAPE VBS enclave, used by Defender's Enhanced Phishing Protection and loaded by LSASS. A repeated call to Initialize wrote a fixed 32-bit value without validating the destination. The researchers corrupted the enclave-range check, then used a ClipboardInput race to gain a controlled memset, which led to VTL1 read and write primitives, replacement of the valid-target table, and arbitrary calls to existing VTL1 code through NtContinue. Microsoft fixed CVE-2026-83498 in September's Patch Tuesday and blocked older SFAPE images through the VBS Code Integrity policy.

infosec.title: Beyond Valid Credentials: How Exposed AWS Keys are Tested for Bedrock Access
infosec.summary: When attackers obtain AWS credentials, they frequently test them for access to other services of interest like SES, SNS, and Bedrock. Datadog examined three credential harvesting platforms and found that they utilize the ListFoundationModels, InvokeModel, and Converse API to determine access. It also found a script that checked for promotional credits available in the account.

infosec.title: Two arrested as DOJ takes down laptop farms responsible for $3 million in North Korean revenue
infosec.summary: The DOJ raided more than 40 Texas residences in late September and seized 187 laptops used by North Korean IT workers, while two US facilitators were arrested for helping funnel over $3 million from about 70 companies. A new FBI advisory said the scheme has adapted, with operatives subcontracting jobs to freelancers in South Asia and West Africa and recruiting financially stressed Americans, including active-duty military, to host laptops or sit interviews. Exposed workers have threatened violence or data leaks to extract payment, and some are now chasing identities that qualify for security-cleared roles.

infosec.title: Modernize application and API security
infosec.summary: Watch this on-demand webinar from AWS and SANS Institute to explore how APIs, cloud-native development, and agentic AI reshape security risks. Learn strategies to evolve threat models, strengthen governance, and adapt controls. Watch now and explore AWS Partner solutions in AWS Marketplace.

infosec.title: CodeGraph
infosec.summary: CodeGraph is a tool to build pre-indexed code knowledge graphs which can be fed to AI agents to speed up code exploration.

infosec.title: Lastwall (Product Launch)
infosec.summary: Lastwall provides identity security for defense and government organizations. Its IDCommand Suite combines zero-trust architecture, PKI, passwordless authentication, and risk scoring from 200 contextual signals. Quantum Shield secures data in transit with NIST-approved post-quantum cryptography.

infosec.title: Security-suite
infosec.summary: A comprehensive open-source security tools suite for OSINT reconnaissance, web security testing, API security assessment, and compliance checking with AI-powered analysis.

infosec.title: Anthropic Warns Self-Replicating AI Could Spread to Your Smart Devices
infosec.summary: Anthropic warns that small AI models could soon self-replicate across consumer IoT devices, creating distributed botnets capable of running AI workloads. Anthropic distributed Gemma4-26B-A4B onto 15 off-brand Android TV boxes but could not demonstrate self-replication. On the hardware in question, inference would be a slow process, so defenders may be able to respond in time to stop any abuse.

infosec.title: AI Regulation Must Mimic Industrial Revolution Laws
infosec.summary: The UK's AI minister, Kanishka Narayan, is drafting plans for compulsory safety reporting and monitoring for frontier AI, and a potential requirement that labs grant pre-release access to models for review. Narayan compared this to the Industrial Revolution and said frontier labs shouldn't release tools they can't guarantee are safe. Narayan also confirmed that he reached an agreement with Anthropic to provide the AISI preview access to Mythos again.

infosec.title: Trezor Wallets Also Compromised with Implants
infosec.summary: Hardware hacker Joe Grand found implants in a Trezor One and a Trezor Model T bought from unauthorized sellers, contradicting Trezor's public claim that none of its devices had been compromised, despite Grand reporting the findings in August. The attackers replaced each device's microcontroller with malicious firmware derived from open source that displayed one of a dozen pre-generated seed phrases while passing integrity checks against a copy of the legitimate firmware stored on an external microSD card. Unlike the Ledger implants, which exfiltrated real seeds over a cellular link, these relied on predictable seeds, and Trezor's move to cut authorized resellers suggested the company feared a similar shift into trusted supply channels.

infosec.title: Racket Infrastructure Compromise

infosec.title: Refrigeration Controller Hack Spoils Food Across European Supermarkets
infosec.summary: Hackers remotely altered Danfoss refrigeration controllers at hundreds of European supermarkets, forcing freezers into defrost for up to six hours.

infosec.title: FBI arrests OpenAI employee for allegedly planting recording device in company offices
infosec.summary: An OpenAI engineer was arrested for allegedly hiding a toilet-paper-wrapped audio recorder in an executive conference room TV's USB port, after a complaint showed he had queried a productivity tool for leadership meeting locations and a chatbot account tied to his spouse had asked how to build and obfuscate the device.

devops.title: SRE book second edition
devops.summary: Google has released a completely rewritten second edition of its Site Reliability Engineering book with O'Reilly Media. The update reflects a decade of changes to the reliability field, including the rise of AI, microservices, and platform engineering. The new text includes guidance on modern challenges like running large language models and using AI to enhance operational reliability.

devops.title: Announcing AWS Lambda Web Functions
devops.summary: AWS Lambda Web Functions is a new form factor that runs standard HTTP web applications without rewriting code into an event handler. Developers can deploy existing Node.js servers built with frameworks like Express or Next.js, and the service automatically handles scaling and multi-region distribution. Each execution environment handles up to 128 concurrent requests, and billing is based on active CPU time rather than total duration. It is available today in five regions.

devops.title: AKS Is Growing – Along With Its Kubernetes Utilization Problem
devops.summary: Per the 2026 State of Kubernetes Optimization Report, AKS CPU utilization fell to 8% and memory to 20%, with CPU overprovisioning at 69%. GPU utilization averages 5% overall and 2% on AKS, driven by conservative resource requests that are rarely revisited.

devops.title: Under the hood, off the hot path: How D1 scales to millions of databases
devops.summary: Cloudflare scaled D1's control plane to manage millions of SQLite-backed databases while keeping centralized components out of the query hot path. Distributed routing metadata, pooled Postgres connections, precomputed aggregations, and idempotent background processes reduce bottlenecks as database counts grow.

devops.title: Headless Observability: The Next Evolution of Autonomous Operations
devops.summary: New Relic argues observability must evolve for AI agents as well as humans, since agents need trusted operational intelligence rather than raw telemetry. Its Ground Truth layer combines telemetry, relationships, evidence, and context, separating intelligence from presentation so dashboards and APIs serve both audiences.

devops.title: Fastest Growing Open Source Datadog Alternative

devops.title: Voicestudio
devops.summary: VoiceStudio is an open-source alternative to ElevenLabs that runs fully locally on user hardware. The software supports voice cloning, video dubbing, transcription, and audiobook creation in 646 languages.

devops.title: Xtool
devops.summary: Xtool is a cross-platform tool that replicates Xcode functionality using open standards. It lets developers build and deploy iOS apps on Linux, Windows, and macOS. The tool can sign, install, and interact with Apple Developer Services programmatically.

devops.title: What gets TOASTed in Postgres
devops.summary: Postgres TOAST compresses oversized variable-length values and moves them into separate storage when necessary. SQL examples show why LZ4's faster compression does not always produce smaller values or faster reads: pglz can outperform it for short previews, while uncompressed external storage can improve reads from the middle of large binary values.

devops.title: Shipping Media Over QUIC at Meta Scale for Instagram Live Ingest
devops.summary: Instagram Live now uses the open standard Media over QUIC (MoQ) protocol for live video ingest on iOS and Android. This switch moves development from Meta's in-house RUSH protocol to a shared IETF standard developed with Google, Akamai, and others. Meta says the MoQ path matched RUSH on streaming quality and reliability measures during testing.

devops.title: Rewinding the exponential: How we keep hardware usage down

Wired's report, drawn from more than two dozen anonymous employees, names tools including ChatGPT, Claude, and image generators. Leadership subscribes to AI tools and runs brainstorming sessions asking staff to find uses, even as the big five sue Meta over copyright.

design.title: Prize-Winning Image Which Sparked Backlash Was AI-Generated, Nikon Rules
design.summary: Nikon has disqualified the winning video of its Small World in Motion microscopy contest, ruling that generative AI used in its composition broke the rules. Scientists, including former judges, had flagged the footage of cilia in a child's airway as fake. The camera-maker is now reviewing the procedures of the annual contest, which has run for 15 years.

design.title: Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm
design.summary: Facebook's new “Your Algorithm” feature lets users describe in their own words what they want to see more or less of in Feed and Reels, with Meta saying recommendations update in real time. An updated three-dot menu provides access to the tool alongside “Interested” and “Not interested” options, and Facebook may ask follow-up questions to understand users' feedback. The launch brings controls already introduced on Instagram to Facebook, giving users a more direct way to shape their recommendations.

design.title: The Fake Double Diamond is Dead. The Real Double Diamond is Immortal
design.summary: Synthetic users and AI-generated insights offer the false certainty of up-front discovery without its substance, and they never remove the need to iterate. Shipping everything and letting analytics decide fails too, because real experiments need a hypothesis, an end point, and cleanup of failed bets. The fake double diamond trades real divergence for synthetic urgency. Useful software needs problem definition and iteration in one shared system.

design.title: What are we willing to sacrifice for AI?
design.summary: If AI eventually allows companies to produce goods and services with far fewer workers, economies built around exchanging labor for income may face a fundamental contradiction. Three broad responses each demand a sacrifice: businesses could preserve jobs at the expense of potential profits, society could restrict AI and forgo some of its benefits, or economic systems could provide guaranteed income or broader ownership while accepting greater institutional dependence. The deeper question is whether existing ideas about liberty and economic independence can survive if meaningful opportunities to earn a living through work become scarce.

design.summary: TypeType's updated TT Rationalist modernizes the slab serif with trapezoidal serifs, softer stroke contrast, humanist proportions, and curved details that make dense text feel less rigid and more comfortable to read. The family spans 22 styles, including ten upright weights, matching true italics, and two variable fonts, with 1,127 glyphs per style and 31 OpenType features. Support for more than 235 Latin- and Cyrillic-based languages makes the family flexible enough for everything from editorial layouts and cultural posters to apps, watch interfaces, and compact digital typography.

design.title: Fix the Contrast without Losing Your Brand
design.summary: Low-contrast text appears on 83.9% of the top million home pages, making it the web's most common accessibility failure. Clearleft's tool “This hue shall pass” maps every pairing in a palette against WCAG AA or AAA and fixes failures by nudging lightness. Hue stays fixed, so brand colors keep their character while passing contrast.

design.title: Pentagram creates dynamic bilingual identity for Design Doha Biennial 2026
design.summary: Pentagram's identity for the 2026 Design Doha Biennial replaces a static logo with a flexible typographic system built around connectivity and equal treatment of Arabic and English. Extended strokes stretch between elements like mapping lines or network constellations, while regional travertine beige and deep maroon are combined with bright orange and the blue established by the inaugural edition. The same structural logic extends across sub-brands and exhibitions, allowing individual programs to develop distinct expressions while remaining part of a coherent bilingual system.

design.title: A' Design Award Winners Achieve Real World Impact through Graphic Design
design.summary: A curated selection of 2026 A' Design Award winners shows graphic design and packaging delivering real-world impact, including Gold winners Aisling Sans and Dotline Corporate Identity.

design.title: The Best Way to Use Icons in Web UIs
design.summary: Icons can be inserted and swapped from CSS alone by storing them as custom-property design tokens and rendering them through masked pseudo-elements.

marketing.summary: Webinar registration isn't the problem, attendance is. But it doesn't have to be. Vidyard's Video in Motion report breaks down the pre-event video strategy getting teams to over 50% attendance rates, complete with blueprint scripts and benchmarks to measure against. marketing.title: Your Algorithm, Your Words: New Ways to Shape What You See on Facebook
marketing.summary: Facebook is using AI to let users shape Feed and Reels recommendations by describing their interests in their own words. Its new “Your” algorithm tool lets users add and manage topics, while expanded feedback options let them explain why they want more or less of certain content. Large language models combine this direct feedback with existing engagement signals to update recommendations in real time, including during the same session.

marketing.title: Meta's TikTok Ad Ban Turns Platform Rivalry Into a Traffic War
marketing.summary: Brands that find creators on TikTok and then use Meta's targeting to reach a wider audience may lose that route, since Meta reportedly now rejects third-party ads that send people to TikTok and other ByteDance properties. The ban took effect October 8 in seven markets, including the US and Canada, and also covers ByteDance's own ad buying on Facebook and Instagram. Campaigns that run across both platforms may now need Meta-native destinations, neutral websites, or separate creative and measurement for each platform.

marketing.title: Show AI influencers with real people
marketing.summary: AI influencers are seen as less trustworthy because they can't actually use the products they promote. Showing them in everyday moments with real people, like grabbing coffee or going for a run, helps close that gap. In a study of 9,500+ posts and 4 experiments, these scenes drove 20.7% more engagement and made people up to 17.5% more likely to choose the product.

marketing.title: How to spot and fix crappy case studies
marketing.summary: B2B case studies often underperform because they document completed projects instead of telling compelling customer stories. Audit your last 3 by checking whether they explain the customer's original problem. If the stories feel interchangeable, interview a customer stakeholder for 30 mins to uncover what went wrong and what improved. 3-5 distinctive case studies can be more persuasive than 20 generic ones. Use anonymous stories when needed and repurpose them across newsletters and social media.

marketing.title: 2026 GURU Conference (Virtual Event)
marketing.summary: This free virtual email and digital marketing event is hosted by Constant Contact on November 12-13. Keynote speakers include actor and writer Molly Ringwald and Emmy-winning creator Dan Levy. Marketing experts Ann Handley, Amy Porterfield, and Jay Schwedelson will share industry insights alongside Kath Pay and Ross Simmonds.

marketing.title: Can I get 3,000 subscribers in 90 days?
marketing.summary: Growth in Public is an experiment by Chenell Basilio to gain 3K email subscribers from social media in 90 days. The site tracks subscriber growth by platform in a live scoreboard and documents which tactics drive signups. After posting just 43 times in the past year and seeing newsletter growth stall, Chenell plans to post daily across LinkedIn and other social platforms to test whether social can become a reliable growth channel again.

marketing.title: What Doesn't Get Cheaper
marketing.summary: AI is making websites cheap enough to build for short-term experiments and one-off events that previously weren't worth the cost. However, enterprise websites still require complex integrations. AI can automate production and support decision-making but cannot eliminate the human effort needed to align stakeholders. Generative tools also create collaboration challenges when multiple companies need to edit the same work. As production costs fall, experimentation will expand while complex projects remain expensive because coordination still requires people.

marketing.title: What Pokemon Pokopia Taught Me About the Future of Marketing
marketing.summary: Creativity comes from experimenting and adapting rather than simply generating a finished result. As AI makes content production faster, marketers risk losing the problem-solving and creative judgment that come from hands-on work. A study in 2024 found AI-assisted stories were rated as more creative but also more similar to one another. To stand out, teams should automate repetitive tasks while protecting time for play and experimentation to develop distinctive taste.

marketing.title: Shopping is part of the product
marketing.summary: AI is changing e-commerce discovery by presenting shoppers with product shortlists instead of sending them to search results. A study on AI Mode found that 74% of participants chose the top-ranked product, while only 10% chose a product ranked third or lower. The author outlines a five-stage organic growth loop: earn AI recommendations through product feeds and third-party signals, convert visitors with tools such as quizzes, encourage user-generated content through packaging and product experiences, generate repeat purchases through customer relationships, and build brand recall. Shopping infrastructure and marketing automation are increasingly table stakes, while customer relationships, creator partnerships, community, first-party data, and brand recall create longer-term advantages.

marketing.title: Duo the owl's next big act is an animated series
marketing.summary: Duolingo is effectively building an entertainment arm around characters that bring in an estimated 15% of new users through organic social.

marketing.title: 32% of US adults prefer highlights over full episodes
marketing.summary: The share rises to 43% among Gen Z, and 37% of Americans say they already use their streaming service more since it added vertical video clips.

founders.title: Why There Will Be More Pro Rata Conflicts
founders.summary: Early-stage funds increasingly exercise pro rata rights across multiple rounds as they grow, driven by outliers offering significant upside potential. The rise of secondary markets and financial vehicles like Fund of Funds and SPVs supports smaller funds in monetizing pro rata shares. Faster round pacing within a fund's investment period further contributes to potential pro rata conflicts.

founders.title: The “alien” economics of AI monetization
founders.summary: Two-thirds of the companies on the Forbes AI 50 list use some form of usage-based pricing. AI's variable costs and unpredictable demand are causing today's leading companies to operate in ways that would seem alien to traditional SaaS businesses. These companies are iterating much faster on pricing, prioritizing market share over ARR, and pursuing multiple go-to-market strategies at once.

founders.title: 38 things we've learned about building AI products
founders.summary: PostHog has built 10 different AI products over the last four years. These include PostHog AI, PostHog's install Wizard, Replay Vision, and Scouts. PostHog's AI products are used by nearly 100,000 people every month. This post details what the company has learned from building them.

founders.title: ARR vs GAAP Revenue | Spotting “ARR” Lies
founders.summary: Businesses need to stay honest about what ARR actually is. If ARR doesn't ultimately lead to revenue and cash, then it's a fake metric. Most companies need to redefine or evolve their definitions of ARR for the AI era. ARR should turn into GAAP revenue, and it shouldn't take a really long time for that to happen.

founders.title: How to Grow a Massive Brand (Full 2026 Masterclass)
founders.summary: A founder's account and a company's account don't need to publish the same things. This guide assigns the founder the beliefs, lessons, and experience of building, while the company explains products and launches. It also distinguishes posts that attract new people from posts that build trust or encourage a purchase. That gives teams a clearer way to judge results: a post meant to introduce the company should not be assessed only by immediate sales. Interested followers can then move into email or a community for a longer relationship.

founders.title: Your business moves fast. So should your money.
founders.summary: Your business moves quickly. Your money should, too. founders.summary: Stripe Workflows now supports recurring schedule triggers. Users choose when a workflow runs, and Stripe starts a run at each scheduled time. Scheduled workflows pair well with list actions and loops. The workflow lives in the Dashboard, so the team that owns the process can read it, change it, and see every run.

founders.title: Gemini 4 Argon available on Google Cloud, built to help solve your business' hardest problems
founders.summary: Gemini 4 Argon is now available on Google Cloud. Argon was trained to work with both depth and precision. It can maintain context across long, multi-step tasks and produce precise, verifiable results. Argon launches with an introductory rate of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens priced at 95% off through to November 30, after which the standard pricing of $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens will apply.

founders.title: Capital Stacks For Atoms
founders.summary: Capital allocation has shifted from bits-based businesses to atoms-based businesses over the last few years. Investors have been directing capital to overcome the physical-world bottlenecks of inference. There's an emerging cohort of atoms-based companies in the fields of energy, manufacturing, space, robotics, and beyond. These hard asset businesses are increasingly built and valued on bundles of cash flows rather than revenue multiples. This requires an entirely different approach to capital formation across the company lifecycle.

founders.title: OK, I might have been wrong about building with a lean team in the age of AI
founders.summary: Chatbase is now at 40 people, and it plans to double its number of employees in the next 6 months. Building is now much easier, and the opportunity cost of not building more is huge. Companies that want to build more, grow more, and achieve more still need to hire because humans are still needed in many parts of the building loop. While this might change, it doesn't make sense to act like it isn't true right now.

founders.title: Friction
founders.summary: AI enables us to do the things we previously procrastinated over.

founders.title: Incentives drive behaviour

founders.summary: Adding more features isn't a guaranteed solution for struggling startups.

founders.title: We hired our way into going slower

founders.title: The Death of Venture Capital's Short Kings
founders.summary: Small VC funds face pressure to grow so they can keep investing in their companies and retain influence in later rounds.

founders.title: Don't diagnose your opponents
founders.summary: Deciding that a colleague opposes your plan because they fear change does not tell you whether their objection is correct.

crypto.title: CFTC's new crypto framework could face a 2028 election deadline
crypto.summary: The CFTC's advance notice on leveraged and margined crypto trading likely will not produce a proposal until late Q1 or early Q2 2027, with finalization not until early 2028, raising the risk the rule never gets finalized before the 2028 election cycle. Fast-tracking would raise the risk of a judge blocking it on procedural grounds, and legal challenges could extend beyond 2028. The proposal would require proof-of-reserves audits and give the CFTC authority over state-licensed platforms.

crypto.title: Binance VIP head says hedge funds are exploring crypto arbitrage
crypto.summary: Catherine Chen, Binance's head of VIP and institutional, said traditional hedge funds are more actively exploring crypto venues, drawn by arbitrage on TradFi instruments such as cash equities and perpetual futures, improved depth, and 24/7 weekend price discovery. She said Binance's cash-equity assets under management rose from about $800-900 million to $1.4 billion, and TradFi perp volume went from $20-30 billion a month at launch to about $400 billion every 30 days, though she called engagement early and said to watch the next 12 to 18 months.

crypto.title: Binance launches AI trading tool
crypto.summary: Binance rolled out its AI-powered trading interface to all global English-language users on October 12, following a beta that drew 150,000 participants over five weeks beginning September 7. The free suite includes AI-generated portfolio summaries, top-mover analysis, voice alerts, on-demand market briefings in text or audio, and a generative UI that adapts displayed market data and tools to each user's stated interests and experience level. The launch extends Binance's super-app strategy, using AI as an onboarding and retention layer for traders who lack the background to interpret raw market data. Additional language support is currently rolling out.

crypto.title: Informed Diffusion: making home builders publish fast
crypto.summary: Informed Diffusion is a four-tier gossip protocol that cuts home-builder payload delivery from 6.3 seconds to 0.63 seconds P99, matching and surpassing the 1.8-second benchmark datacenter builders achieve on mixed-bandwidth networks. Pipelining, push/pull chunk announcement, erasure coding, and neighbor-aware scheduling via per-payload HAVE bitmaps reduce bandwidth utilization from 4.4 to 1.7 payload copies and hold delivery under the 3-second budget against 50% withholding nodes, 10 Mbps throttled uplinks, and payloads ranging from 128 KiB to 2 MiB. The sole wire protocol addition is HAVE bitmaps carried in existing gossipsub control messages, with all other improvements left to local client implementation, allowing adoption without mesh topology changes or new topics.

crypto.title: NFT marketplace Blur is shutting down after volumes collapse 99%
crypto.summary: Blur will close its marketplace and lending arm Blend on November 12 after monthly Ethereum NFT trading volume fell 99.5% from its March 2023 peak of $1.43 billion, when the platform held over 70% of ETH NFT market share, to under $7 million. Token Terminal records zero protocol revenue across three years of operation, as Blur charged no transaction fees throughout its run, a model that built dominant volume but left no economic foundation. The shutdown follows Blast network's closure by ten days, with both projects built by Tieshun Roquerre (Pacman), and Blast's TVL having fallen from $2 billion to roughly $32 million before its team cited unsustainable operational costs. The BLUR token dropped over 20% on the announcement, trading around $0.015.

crypto.title: The Death of the Interface
crypto.summary: David Marcus, who led Meta's M assistant and Libra and now runs Lightspark, argues that AI models and stablecoin law have finally arrived together, so apps, websites, and buttons will give way to agents you simply talk to. Payments today assume a human in the loop (checkout pages, texted codes, fraud, and dispute flows), so money must stop moving through a UI. Stablecoins are no longer a standalone category. To be useful, they need fast settlement networks, embedded wallets, fiat connectivity, and card networks, which he calls “headless money,” a simple API that agents can use to move value anywhere, 24/7, with revocable spending limits and clear liability for mistakes. A few payment-stack companies will be worth hundreds of billions, but the companies running the winning agents will earn far more, since payment stacks earn only 1 to 300 basis points.

crypto.title: Crypto Trader 'Realist' Reports Knifepoint Robbery at UK Home
crypto.summary: UK-based crypto trader 'Realist' reported a knifepoint home robbery valued at approximately $800,000, with on-chain records corroborating the claim via 719,000 USDC transferred through an identified Solana address. The incident extends a documented pattern of physical attacks targeting traders whose wallet balances and identities are linkable onchain. Attackers use blockchain transparency to identify high-value targets, then coerce asset transfers through physical force rather than technical exploits. This attack category, sometimes called a "$5 wrench attack," bypasses cryptographic security and poses a growing physical threat to high-net-worth on-chain participants.

crypto.title: Robinhood Reports $15B in Stock Token Trading as Chain Passes 100 Days
crypto.summary: Robinhood's blockchain crossed 100 days of operation with $15 billion in stock token trading volume and 200,000 token holders, placing the platform among the largest tokenized-equity deployments by a regulated broker. Morpho's deployment on the chain has drawn approximately $1.1 billion in deposits, demonstrating that DeFi lending primitives can attract meaningful TVL when layered on top of tokenized equity infrastructure. The combined metrics, trading volume plus onchain credit demand, suggest users are treating tokenized stocks as composable collateral rather than purely buy-and-hold instruments.

crypto.title: Aave App crosses $30M in deposits in under two months
crypto.summary: The Aave App passed $30 million in deposits less than two months after launch, indicating that banks could eventually launch their own frontends on Aave.

crypto.title: US government's 17,733 BTC transfers were likely custody-related
crypto.summary: US government-linked wallets moved about 17,733 BTC to Coinbase Prime in early October, including 12,267 BTC tied to the Bitfinex hack, with labeled government holdings falling from 324,527 to 306,795 BTC.

crypto.title: South Korea orders website blocks on 27 unregistered foreign exchanges
crypto.summary: South Korea's FIU said regulators ordered domestic access blocks on 27 unregistered overseas crypto exchange sites, including KuCoin, MEXC, Phemex, Bitrue, Poloniex, BTCC, BingX, and BitMart, after reviews on October 6 and 7.

Read it to see how: Ungoverned AI is the risk that compounds every other one Model risk does not end at deployment Vendor-embedded agents can access enterprise systems without appearing in your inventory Most organizations cannot say who approved an agent's decision, or who was responsible for the policy behind it Download your report

it.title: Microsoft to expand Azure Maia system to multi-gigawatt deployments
it.summary: Microsoft has announced plans to expand its Azure Maia custom silicon system to multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027, making Maia the primary inference system for its products. Maia 200 is currently in production for workloads such as Microsoft Copilot, while the upcoming Maia 300 architecture is designed to deliver significant efficiency and throughput gains for long-context and multi-step agentic AI tasks.

it.title: Intel optimizes IPv6 networking into nothingness, say users
it.summary: Users are reporting IPv6 connectivity failures linked to Intel Connectivity Performance Suite, causing intermittent problems with services including OneDrive and OneNote. Removing or updating the problematic software has resolved reported issues, highlighting how vendor networking utilities can create difficult-to-diagnose enterprise connectivity problems.

it.title: Human PR Review is Next
it.summary: AI-generated code is making traditional line-by-line human PR reviews less practical, shifting quality assurance toward automated checks, guardrails, and test-driven verification. Developers can maintain code quality without reading the implementation by using pre-code rules, multi-model review bots, and user acceptance testing.

it.title: No Room for Bugs
it.summary: Software-correctness tools reduce the space for bugs through three approaches: raising the floor with correct-by-construction features like type systems and memory safety, pushing the walls inward with verification tools like SMT solvers, and detecting remaining bugs through model checking and fuzzing. Tools that rely on separate models risk implementation drift, where the model no longer matches the actual code. Hydro addresses this limitation by running correctness checks directly against deployed code.

it.title: 6 IT wins to deliver before the year ends
it.summary: IT leaders share the initiatives they are prioritizing in the final quarter, from delivering previously committed projects to demonstrating measurable business value. The recommendations emphasize finishing meaningful work, improving productivity, and establishing credibility for next year's investments.

it.title: Who made the request? AI agents need identity context
it.summary: Alice tells an AI agent, “List my customers.” The agent calls the MCP tool: get_customer_list_tool. Alice isn't mentioned. (The MCP doesn't know who Alice is, anyway.) Teleport explains how to carry identity through the agent – securely and temporarily using JWTs. Read the blog →

it.title: Broadcom Introduces VMware HyperArmor, Expanding Hypervisor Security and Protections for VMware Cloud Foundation
it.summary: Broadcom's VMware HyperArmor protects VMware Cloud Foundation hypervisors against AI-accelerated cyberattacks, stolen credentials, and unpatched vulnerabilities. It combines virtual patching, application allowlisting, and hypervisor-level MFA to block threats without requiring downtime, software upgrades, or guest VM agents.

it.title: Workday to Acquire C1.ai, a Leading Agentic Identity Platform for People and Agents
it.summary: Workday has announced an agreement to acquire C1.ai, expanding into identity governance for employees and AI agents. The proposed integration would connect employee lifecycle events directly to application provisioning, permission changes, and access removal across enterprise systems.

it.title: Apple unleashes a swarm of Mac Minions to share GPU resources for large AI tasks
it.summary: Apple researchers have developed Minions, a distributed system that pools unused GPU capacity across Apple Silicon Macs for AI workloads. The approach has reportedly reduced some internal inference job wait times from more than ten hours to minutes.

it.title: Can we change an AI model's architecture without retraining it from scratch?
it.summary: Amazon Web Services researchers have introduced priming, a method that reuses pretrained Transformer weights to reduce the pretraining cost of hybrid state space models by over 99%. The technique addresses the Transformer memory tax by replacing certain attention layers with state space layers like Gated KalmaNet, which researchers found can match source Transformer reasoning benchmarks while decoding up to twice as quickly. To foster further research, the team released a zoo of primed hybrid models, training code, and a vLLM serving plugin under the Apache 2.0 License.

it.title: Find your routine next steps on the post-meeting screen in Google Meet
it.summary: Google Meet is introducing Gemini-powered post-meeting routines that can automatically draft follow-up emails and export action items to Google Tasks when meeting notes are enabled.

it.title: Chaos or death
it.summary: Successful AI adoption requires sustained leadership, clear decision-making, and established routines to manage growing organizational complexity, as AI makes disorder easier to create without reducing the effort needed to maintain order.

hardware.title: Introducing AMD Helion, Agentic AI Compute at Rack Scale
hardware.summary: AMD's Helion agentic AI rack is designed for flexible AI infrastructure that caters to hyperscale deployments and enterprise needs. It supports a range of configurations, including CPU-only and GPU-integrated systems, aligning with diverse AI workloads. Helion, part of an upcoming open blueprint by AMD for OCP, is set for release in November.

Digitimes reports that the supply chain is already preparing for a surge in server builds in 2027.

hardware.title: Building a GPU compiler from scratch, from PyTorch to CUDA

It uses RMSNorm and matrix multiplication as worked examples. It also covers operator fusion, schedule selection, and online attention rewrites, so readers can see what Triton-style stacks do under the hood.

hardware.summary: Physical Intelligence opened a beta API for its π robotics foundation models: upload demonstrations, fine-tune on Pi-managed compute, and run the result on your own robot through a hosted inference gateway. Early partners spanned hardware from Actor's autonomous wheel loader, running a commercial deployment with no operator onboard, to Almond's dual-arm Axol, which learned to deburr its own spacers in four days. Since most ran cloud-hosted inference, network connectivity was a pain point for some.

hardware.summary: Apple Silicon Macs have powerful GPUs that sit mostly idle in normal use.
